escalation.rationale: Trump signals imminent decision on resuming large-scale Iran strikes, Houthis execute largest land grab in years threatening Saudi oil infrastructure, IRGC strikes oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz, and Poland warns of deliberate Russian 'accidental' attacks designed to test NATO Article 5 — sustaining near-critical multi-theater pressure.

ticker_items: Trump weighs resuming major Iran strikes ahead of Gulf leader talks at UNGA.
IRGC strikes oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media report.
Houthis seize territory near key Saudi oil corridor; fuel prices spike globally.
Poland PM Tusk warns Russia planning 'accidental' strikes on NATO allies.
Russia strikes Zaporizhzhia shopping center; UN mission finds US strike on Iran school a likely war crime.

eastern_europe.description: Russian strike set a shopping center ablaze in Zaporizhzhia, heightening civilian infrastructure targeting concerns.

middle_east.description: IRGC struck an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian media reports cited by Haaretz.
UN mission found grounds to believe the US committed a war crime in a strike on a primary school in Minab killing approximately 155 people.
UN mission cited a US strike on a sports centre in Lamerd killing 22 people as a potential war crime.

middle_east.target_location: Southern Saudi Arabia / Yemen border region
middle_east.description: Houthis executed their largest land grab in years, threatening Saudi oil export corridors and reigniting Yemen's civil war.

observers.description: PM Robert Fico publicly warned that the West is seeking a pretext for a major Russia-NATO war, positioning Slovakia as a dissenting NATO voice. Fico continues to resist full alignment with Western escalatory posture toward Russia.

PM Donald Tusk issued a stark warning that Russia is planning deliberate 'accidental' attacks on NATO allies to test Article 5 solidarity. Poland remains one of the most forward-leaning NATO states on eastern flank defense, hosting Multi-Domain Command – Europe assets.

President Lee Jae Myung confirmed Seoul will not deploy troops to the Strait of Hormuz or participate militarily in the US-Iran war. South Korea signaled willingness to facilitate US-North Korea diplomatic dialogue as Trump reportedly seeks Pyongyang engagement.

Gen. Jennie Carignan is competing for the NATO Military Committee chair in a secret ballot vote, which could significantly elevate Canada's institutional role in the alliance. The US-Canada relationship under Trump introduces uncertainty about Washington's support for her candidacy.

Turkey revoked the operating licence of Iran's Bank Mellat in Istanbul, a significant financial enforcement step aligned with Western sanctions pressure. Ankara continues to balance NATO commitments with independent economic ties to both Russia and Iran.

Saudi oil infrastructure faces direct threat from the Houthi land offensive, and reports suggest Riyadh is exploring backchannel feelers with Ansar Allah. Saudi Arabia is seeking to restore East-West pipeline capacity as Houthi pressure on export routes intensifies.

financial.brent_crude: Elevated — supply fears from Houthi Saudi oil threat partially offset by East-West pipeline restoration efforts; WTI down ~$1.75 on the day
financial.notes: Crude prices remain volatile: WTI fell ~$1.75 on Saudi pipeline restoration hopes but Houthi offensive near Saudi oil corridors and IRGC tanker strike in Hormuz continue to sustain upward supply-risk premium.
